mosaic

moh-ZAY-ik — stress on second syllable · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A mosaic is a picture or design created by fitting together many small pieces of colored stone, glass, or tile.

The courtyard floor was a mosaic of tiny blue and gold tiles forming a peacock.

Example

An artist collects fragments of broken pottery and colored glass from a demolished building and fits each piece snugly against the next in a frame, until the fragments become a striking mosaic of a flying bird.

Mosaic is precise here because it emphasizes not just that there is a picture or design, but specifically that it is made by fitting together many small, distinct pieces. Simply saying "picture" or "design" would miss the crucial element of assembly from fragments.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

picture: A picture is any image made to be viewed, however it was produced — painted, drawn, printed, or photographed. A mosaic is one very particular kind of picture: an image built up from many small, separate pieces of colored stone, glass, or tile fitted tightly together.

composition: A composition is any arrangement of parts into a whole — the word fits a song, an essay, or a painting equally well. A mosaic is far more specific: its parts are small, hard pieces of stone, glass, or tile, and the whole is a picture they form when fitted together.

tapestry: A tapestry is a picture woven from colored threads on a loom, all of it one continuous piece of cloth. A mosaic builds its picture the opposite way, out of many separate hard fragments — stone, glass, or tile — fitted edge to edge. Woven thread versus assembled pieces is the difference.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

monolith: a single, massive, undivided block

uniformity: total sameness, with no variety of parts

Where it sits · how precisely pieces form one design — fragment → arrangement → collage → mosaic

fragment vs. mosaic: A fragment is just one broken piece — the smallest unit, far below a mosaic, which unites thousands of such pieces into a single picture.

arrangement vs. mosaic: An arrangement is any orderly grouping, but a mosaic is a precise, artistic arrangement in which every small tile locks into a larger design.

collage vs. mosaic: A collage is pieces pasted together loosely, while a mosaic is the most exacting version: small hard tiles fitted tightly together to form one polished image.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — mosa (musa)

Root — mosa (musa): of the Muses, the Greek goddesses of art (Latin, from Greek Mousa)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: forms a noun or adjective meaning 'relating to'

Put it together

Put it together: The root traces to the Muses, the Greek goddesses of art and inspiration: a mosaic was 'work worthy of the Muses' — an artwork painstakingly assembled from many small colored pieces of stone, glass, or tile.

Use the root in a new word: museum

Use the root in a new word: museum: A museum was originally a 'home of the Muses,' the Greek goddesses of the arts — and a mosaic was artwork fine enough to honor those same Muses.

Word Choice

neutral / artistic

Mosaic is a precise art word: it names a picture assembled from many small, distinct pieces of tile, glass, or stone. Reach for it when the fitting-together of fragments is the point. If you only mean an image in general, the plain words "picture" or "design" are the simpler choice.
